proposed_widenings.name: form_transformation
proposed_widenings.justification: Shapechange replaces the caster's entire stat block with another creature's stat block while retaining a specific set of personal attributes. No existing spell family or OngoingOperation variant can express this — ongoing_effect only supports roll_modifier and damage_on_hit operations. A new family (or new operation kind) is needed for the stat-block-adoption + attribute-retention pattern shared by Shapechange, Polymorph, and True Polymorph.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Your game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the chosen form, but you retain your creature type; alignment; personality; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; proficiencies; and ability to communicate.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_temp_hp
proposed_widenings.justification: Shapechange grants Temporary Hit Points equal to the first form's HP on cast. Temp HP is mechanically distinct from regular HP healing — they form a separate pool, do not stack, and vanish at spell end. The current heal_hp effect atom covers HP restoration only. A separate grant_temp_hp atom is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you cast the spell, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to the Hit Points of the first form into which you shape-shift. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the spell ends.

proposed_widenings.name: mid_spell_form_change_activation
proposed_widenings.justification: The caster can use the Magic action during the spell's duration to adopt a different eligible form. This is a repeatable, mid-spell re-activation that costs a Magic action and re-applies the stat-block replacement. The current surface has no mechanism for ongoing spells that allow repeated activation of a sub-effect via a standard action cost while the parent concentration is held.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You shape-shift into another creature for the duration or until you take a Magic action to shape-shift into a different eligible form.

notes: Shapechange's core mechanic — adopting another creature's stat block while selectively retaining personal attributes — has no honest home in the current four spell families. forcing it into ongoing_effect would require inventing an operation kind not in the closed OngoingOperation union. The temp HP on cast and the repeatable mid-spell form change are additional gaps. All three widenings are required together for an honest encoding. This pattern is shared with Polymorph (level 4) and True Polymorph (level 9), suggesting a form_transformation family is worth formalizing.
